description: A thicket of arching, prickly red-brown canes 1-2.5 m tall with leaves of five to seven toothed leaflets, clear pink five-petalled flowers in late spring and early summer, and round red hips that stay on the bare canes into winter. It grows where the ground stays damp, along creeks, swales, seeps and the shady edges of oak woodland, and its tangles shelter quail and rabbits while its hips feed birds, foxes, coyotes and bears.

season_notes.winter: Bare red-brown canes, prickly, still hung with shiny red hips that birds and foxes pick through the winter.
season_notes.spring: New leaves in March, fresh and bright green; the first pink flowers open in May.
season_notes.summer: Pink roses 3-5 cm across, a few at a time, into July, busy with bees; green hips swell behind them.
season_notes.fall: Hips turn red-orange; the leaves go yellow and dull red and drop by late November.

notes: California wild rose is a deciduous shrub 1-2.5 m (occasionally to 3 m) that spreads by suckers into thickets on moist ground: creek banks, swales, valley floors, seeps and the shaded edges of oak woodland, from the valley into the lower conifer belt. Form: plain 'shrub'. Seven to twelve slender canes from the base (stems [7, 12], radius_ratio 0.009, much thinner than the evergreen shrubs) lean out widely (stem_spread 56) and arch over (trunk curve 24, level-1 droop 10), so the clump is a rounded tangle wider than tall, leafy nearly to the ground (envelope base 0.46, foliage start 0.02). Old thickets get a class of their own with many canes and grey dead ones inside. Canes red-brown to grey with stout, often curved prickles (not modelled: they are far below a card's resolution); twig_rgb is the red-brown of young canes. Leaves alternate, pinnately compound, 5-10 cm, with five to seven finely toothed oval leaflets 1.5-3.5 cm: leaf_shape pinnate_compound, leaf_size_m 0.09 for the whole leaf, leaflets [5, 7], leaflet_ratio 0.3; leaf_fill 1.6 because a card holds few compound leaves. Flowers single or in small clusters of a few, five petals, clear pink, 3-5 cm, May to July (some into August): flowers cluster, size_m 0.05 for a small group. Hips round, about 1-1.5 cm, with a short neck, red-orange from August, and they hang on the bare canes through winter: berries months [8, 2], which the generator's month test wraps across the new year (decoActive), so the hips show on the bare-crown texture from December to February as well. Leaves out in March, yellow and dull red in October and November, bare December-February (leaf_on_by_month); winter_twigs 0.55 because a bare rose thicket is a dense mass of canes. Architectural model provisional. Lineup 2026-10-29: the canes took 732 of 1,000 near triangles; 6-10 canes and a budget of 1,300.
